entries.title: An unexpected opening
entries.literal_meaning: As when the hanging sling breaks to the cat’s good fortune.
entries.explanation: Something previously out of reach becomes available by chance. The cat benefits from a broken hanging food sling, rather than from a plan of its own.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହା ଆଗରୁ ପହଞ୍ଚ ବାହାରେ ଥିଲା, ତାହା ହଠାତ୍ ମିଳିଗଲେ ଏହି କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A cancellation unexpectedly frees a place on a fully booked course. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ଶିକା denotes a rope support for suspended vessels; its separate dictionary entry explains this comparison.

entries.title: Beyond a ruler’s favour
entries.odia: କପାଳେ ନ ଥିଲେ ଭୂପାଳେ ନ ଦିଅନ୍ତି
entries.literal_meaning: If it is not in one’s fate, even the ruler does not give it.
entries.explanation: The saying voices resignation when hoped-for help fails. It expresses a belief about fate, not proof that effort or assistance is useless.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଶା କରିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନ ମିଳିଲେ ଭାଗ୍ୟକୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେଇ ଏହି କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A hoped-for recommendation brings no result. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source places this under the fate sense of କପାଳ.

entries.title: Already humiliated
entries.odia: ମୋତେ ମାରନାଁ ମୁଁ ମଲିଣି, ଦୀପ ଲଗେଇ ଦେଖ୍ ପିଠି, ଲାଉ ଚୋର ଭାବ ପାଇଲିଣି
entries.literal_meaning: Do not hit me; I am already dead. Light a lamp and look at my back: I have acquired the name of a gourd thief.
entries.explanation: The dictionary uses this under humiliation: punishment and disgrace have already landed. The protest is not permission for further violence.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅପମାନ ଓ ଦଣ୍ଡ ସହିସାରିଥିବା ଲୋକର ପ୍ରତିବାଦ ଏଠାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A fictional speaker protests against being shamed again. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: No actual theft or punishment incident is verified.

entries.title: One thing tended, another neglected
entries.odia: ଆମ୍ୱ ଗଛରେ ପାଣି ଦଉଁ ଦଉଁ ଶିମ୍ୱ ଗଛ ମଲା
entries.literal_meaning: While watering the mango tree, the bean plant died.
entries.explanation: Attention given to one concern can leave another unattended. This is an editorial reading of the contrast, not gardening advice.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୋଟିଏ କାମରେ ଲାଗି ଅନ୍ୟ କାମକୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏଥିରେ ଦିଶେ।
entries.usage_example: Preparing a presentation, someone forgets a smaller urgent task. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary supplies the withering sense; no origin story.

entries.title: When speaking feels unsafe
entries.odia: କହିବି ତା ଆଗେ ଶୁଣିବେ କେ? ଘଇତା ଅବୁଝା ମାରିବ ଯେ
entries.literal_meaning: I would tell him—but who will listen? The uncomprehending husband will hit me.
entries.explanation: The speaker fears that a complaint will bring violence instead of a hearing. The saying exposes a situation in which someone feels unheard and unsafe; it does not make that treatment acceptable.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା କହିଲେ ଶୁଣିବା ବଦଳରେ ମାଡ଼ ମିଳିବ ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତା ଭୟ କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଏହା ଅସହାୟତାର କଥା, ହିଂସାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: In a fictional discussion, this line names the fear of being punished for speaking up. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ଘଇତା means husband here. The gendered scene belongs to this witness, not a claim about all husbands or households.

entries.title: Habit while the house floods
entries.odia: ଘର ବୁଡ଼ି ପାଣି ଆଣ୍ଠୁଏ ହେଲାଣି ପୁଅଙ୍କର ପିକା ଖିଆ ଛାଡ଼ ଯାଉ ନାହିଁ
entries.literal_meaning: The house is flooded knee-deep, yet the fellow cannot give up smoking his cheroot.
entries.explanation: The image mocks someone who clings to a habit while an urgent problem grows around him. The dictionary marks ପୁଅ here as a satirical reference to a person, not necessarily a child.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଡ଼ ବିପଦ ଆସିଥିଲେ ବି ନିଜ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ଛାଡ଼ି କାମରେ ଲାଗୁ ନଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ଏହି କଥା ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: A team faces an urgent deadline while someone keeps refreshing an entertainment feed. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The separate ପିକା entry identifies a cheroot. No smoking practice is recommended.

entries.title: A hare’s horn
entries.explanation: The expression names something impossible or unreal. Its force comes from looking for a feature the animal does not possess.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହା ନାହିଁ ବା ସମ୍ଭବ ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାକୁ ବୁଝାଇବାକୁ ‘ଶଶ ବିଷାଣ’ କୁହାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Someone asks for a plan with unlimited benefits and no cost or trade-off. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly explains figurative use and lists related impossible images. It is semantically related to existing ଆକାଶକୁସୁମ, but has a distinct image and wording.
